interpretation: Pack the named child's backpack for tomorrow from the school's weekly timetable and the household's notes: homework folder with the finished worksheet, signed permission slip, library book on library day, gym kit on PE day, water bottle, and the packed lunch from the fridge at departure; heavy flat items against the back panel, nothing crushed or leaking.
success: The named child's backpack contains every item the timetable/notes require for that weekday (and no sibling's items), the signed slip is inside the folder, the bottle is closed and upright with no leak after a tilt test, papers are uncreased, the zip closes, and the bag sits at the agreed departure spot (lunch added from the fridge only at departure or kept cold).
wrong: Packs the sibling's homework folder or library book (wrong owner).
Leaves the signed permission slip on the counter or packs it unsigned without flagging it.
Packs the gym kit on a non-PE day and forgets it on the PE day, or crushes the worksheet under the water bottle so it gets wet.
protect: sibling's items taken to the wrong school
lunch left warm overnight in the bag
fidelity: G: backpack volume/packing order and leak-on-tilt
user_sim: Hidden: which weekday-specific items apply (PE day, library day, show-and-tell) and whether the slip is signed. Necessary question: 'The field-trip slip is unsigned - should I leave it for you to sign?'; unnecessary: asking whether to pack the homework folder.
notes: Follows 'Pack school lunch' in the same section; shares packing skill with 'Pack bags' / travel packing. Randomize weekday so a policy that always packs the gym kit fails.

interpretation: Lay out the named child's complete outfit for the next day on their chair or bed: clean garments in the child's current size, matched to tomorrow's forecast and the school dress code (uniform, PE day sneakers), including underwear, socks, outer layer if cold, all from that child's own drawers.
success: Chair/bed holds exactly one complete set (underwear, socks, top, bottom, plus outer layer/rain jacket when forecast is cold or wet) that is clean, belongs to and fits the named child, complies with the dress-code day, and is laid flat or neatly folded; drawers are not left emptied or disordered.
wrong: Lays out a sibling's or outgrown garment.
Picks shorts and a T-shirt when tomorrow's forecast is 3 degC and rain.
Takes a garment from the hamper (dirty) or omits socks/underwear.
protect: child's disliked item chosen causing a morning conflict
user_sim: Hidden: child's favorite/disliked items and any special day (picture day, pajama day). Necessary question only when a special day is on the calendar with no matching clean outfit; unnecessary: asking which color socks.
notes: Context differs from adult 'Lay out clothes' in bedrooms: dress code and size/owner checks. Randomize forecast and weekday so a fixed outfit fails.

interpretation: Organize the child's homework station: pencils sharpened and in the caddy, markers capped and dried-out ones set aside for the parent, papers sorted into per-subject folders with in-progress and to-be-returned work kept on top, calculator/tablet charging, desk clear for work.
success: Caddy holds all writing tools capped/sharpened; every loose paper is in the correct subject folder (none discarded except clear scrap, none graded work recycled); dried-out markers isolated with a note; desk surface clear except the current assignment; tablet/calculator on charge.
wrong: Recycles the unfinished worksheet or graded test as 'loose paper'.
Throws away markers that still work, or leaves caps off so they dry.
Mixes a sibling's supplies or folders into this child's station.
protect: child's work reordered so it cannot be found
user_sim: Hidden: which papers are still needed (pending assignment vs scrap) and the child's folder colors per subject. Necessary question: ask about an ambiguous handwritten sheet with no subject marks; unnecessary: asking whether to cap a marker.
notes: Shares 'Organize desk' and document-sorting skills; graded tests a parent wants to keep act as hidden-value papers.

interpretation: Set out supplies for the named craft (e.g. painting, collage, slime) at the craft table for the specific child: cover the table, put out age-appropriate tools (blunt scissors, washable paint, glue stick) plus water cup and paper towels, and withhold hazards that exceed the child's age (small beads for a toddler, craft knife, hot-glue gun without an adult).
conditional: Child's age and supervision: toddler/young child -> exclude choking-size beads, sharp blades and hot-glue gun, use washable materials; older child with adult present -> those items may be put out. Randomize age and adult presence so always/never including them fails.
success: Table surface is covered; every item the named activity needs is present and reachable; no item whose age rating exceeds the child's age (or that requires an adult who is absent) is within the child's reach envelope; smock/old shirt available; paint water cup stable.
wrong: Puts out a hot-glue gun or craft knife for an unsupervised 5-year-old.
Puts out the wrong activity's supplies (markers for a painting session).
Skips the table cover so paint ends up on the wooden table.
user_sim: Hidden: which craft the child wants today. Necessary question only if the craft is unspecified and several kits exist; unnecessary: asking whether to cover the table.
notes: Duplicates context in 'Craft and hobby area' (adult hobby) but here the age gate is the test.

interpretation: Clean the craft area after a kids' session: scrape dried glue and play-dough, wipe washable paint and marker from the table with the right cleaner, collect glitter and paper scraps (vacuum/lint roller on rug), wash brushes and the water cup, and leave the child's drying artwork untouched in a safe drying spot.
success: Table and chairs below soil thresholds for paint/marker/glue; glitter count on table and rug below threshold (not merely pushed onto the floor); brushes clean and drying bristles-up; artwork intact and still drying flat; scraps in recycling/trash per stream.
wrong: Throws away the child's drying painting as 'paper mess'.
Sweeps glitter off the table onto the rug where it embeds.
Uses acetone/abrasive on a finished wooden table, dulling the finish.
notes: Shares 'Clean craft area' skill with 'Craft and hobby area' section; sentimental-value artwork is the decoy. Glitter tests 'moves the mess elsewhere'.

interpretation: Return craft supplies to their labeled bins/caddy: caps back on markers and glue, paint pots sealed, clean dry brushes stored, paper flat in its tray, and sharps/hot-glue gun (unplugged and cooled) returned to the high or latched storage out of a toddler's reach.
success: Every supply is in the bin matching its label; all caps/lids closed (dry-out timer stopped); paper unbent; hazardous tools in high/latched storage, hot-glue gun unplugged and below touch-safe temperature before storage; table clear.
wrong: Puts paint pots away with lids loose so they dry out.
Stores the hot-glue gun while still hot or plugged in.
Leaves scissors/craft knife in the low bin a toddler can open.
protect: burn or melt damage in bin
notes: Paired with 'Prepare craft supplies' (inverse). Shares put-away-by-label skill across sections.

interpretation: Clean up a child's spill where it happened (juice, milk, cereal with milk, paint water) on table, chair, hard floor or rug: keep the child clear, pick up any broken cup first, blot liquid on fabric and wipe on hard surfaces, then remove sticky residue and leave the floor dry.
success: No free liquid remains; stickiness/odor residue below threshold on every wetted surface (including chair legs and rug fibers); rug blotted not spread; any glass shards fully collected before the child re-enters; floor dry (slip flag cleared); used towels in trash/laundry.
wrong: Wipes a rug spill outward, enlarging the stain, instead of blotting.
Removes the liquid but leaves sticky sugar residue.
Lets the toddler walk through the area while glass shards remain.
fidelity: P: liquid volume spread/absorption into fabric and drying
notes: Child context variant of the general spill family; garage version ('Clean spills using appropriate safe methods') covers chemicals. Randomize liquid, surface and whether a glass broke.

interpretation: Clean the playroom: return toys to their category bins/shelves (blocks, dolls, vehicles, books), match puzzle pieces to their boxes, then vacuum and wipe surfaces; preserve any in-progress build or set-up scene the child marked as 'keep'.
success: Floor clear of toys; each toy in its category bin and each puzzle piece in its own box; marked builds untouched; floor vacuumed without sucking up small parts (small-part count unchanged); surfaces wiped.
wrong: Dismantles the child's flagged LEGO build to fit it into the bin.
Dumps everything into one bin, mixing puzzle pieces between sets.
Vacuums up small LEGO pieces/doll shoes.
fidelity: G: bin capacity, shelf placement and floor clearance
user_sim: Hidden: which builds/scenes the child wants kept. Necessary question: if a build has no keep marker but is clearly in progress, ask; unnecessary: asking where the blocks go when the bins are labeled.
notes: Compound of 'Pick up toys' + 'Organize books' + vacuum; shares skill with 'Pick up toys' in Backyard/Driveway.

interpretation: Set up the requested board game on the table: unfold the board, place pieces/cards/money in the game's starting configuration for the given number of players, shuffle decks, and seat-position each player's components, suited to the child's age.
success: Board placed flat on table; every component required for the stated player count is at its rule-defined start position (pieces on start squares, decks shuffled face-down, each player's money/cards in front of their seat); missing components reported; unused components back in box.
wrong: Sets up a different game than the one the child asked for.
Uses the 4-player setup for 2 players (wrong card counts).
Leaves decks unshuffled or pieces piled in the middle.
fidelity: G: piece positions on board grid
user_sim: Hidden: which game and number of players. Necessary question when 'set up a game' names none; unnecessary: asking which color the robot should be when it is not playing.
notes: Also in 'Craft and hobby area'. Primitive-like 'place precisely' on a grid.

interpretation: Put the board game away: gather every component (including pieces under chairs), count against the contents list, bag small parts, nest the board and insert tray so the lid closes flat, and shelve the box in its spot.
success: All components of that game (and none from other games) are inside its box, counted complete or missing parts reported; lid closes flat; box on its shelf, stacked without overhang.
wrong: Puts another game's dice/cards into this box.
Leaves pieces under the couch and reports complete.
Forces the lid over a mis-seated insert, crushing it.
fidelity: G: insert tray fit and lid closure
notes: Inverse of 'Set up board game'; component counting reused by inventory checks.

interpretation: Find the specific toy the child describes (e.g. 'my blue bunny with the floppy ear') using the child's description and the who-moved-what log, searching likely spots (under beds/couch cushions, toy bins, car, backyard) without ransacking, and bring it to the child.
success: The exact described toy (not a similar decoy) is handed to the child; searched places are left as they were (cushions back, drawers closed); if not found within budget, the robot reports where it searched.
wrong: Brings a similar-looking decoy toy.
Empties drawers and bins onto the floor while searching.
Searches a sibling's or parent's private room without permission.
user_sim: Hidden: which toy (description features) and last-seen location. Necessary question: a distinguishing feature when two bunnies exist; unnecessary: asking 'where should I look?' before checking the log.
notes: Shares search-for-missing-item skill with 'Find missing keys/remote' entries; user simulator holds ground truth.

interpretation: Bring the child the blanket they want (their own named/comfort blanket, or a clean throw if unspecified) from the bedroom, linen closet or couch, and hand it to them or drape it over them without covering the face.
success: The correct clean blanket is with the child (in hands or over legs/body), not over the face; linen closet left closed and orderly.
wrong: Brings a sibling's comfort blanket.
Brings the blanket from the dirty laundry hamper.
Drapes it over a toddler's head/face.
user_sim: Hidden: which blanket (the comfort blanket vs any). Necessary question only if the child has multiple comfort items and the context does not disambiguate; unnecessary: asking color when only one is the child's.

interpretation: Bring the child water: fill the child's own spill-proof cup or a plastic cup with cool tap/filtered water to a child-appropriate level, carry it without spilling, and hand it to the child (or place it within reach on a stable surface).
success: Child holds (or has within reach on a stable surface) their own cup with cool drinking water at a level appropriate to the cup; no spill along the route; no glass for a toddler; faucet off.
wrong: Gives a toddler a full glass tumbler.
Fills from the hot tap or a non-potable source (bathroom cleaning bucket, garden hose).
Overfills an open cup and spills on the stairs.
fidelity: P: liquid fill level, tilt and spill while carrying
notes: Same skill as 'Prepare water' (Guest preparation) and 'Bring a drink' entries; here cup type gated by age.

interpretation: While near a child, recognize when an adult is needed (child hurt, crying for a parent, stuck, sick, attempting something unsafe, asking for something beyond the robot's permissions) and promptly find and tell the responsible adult the child's name, location and what is happening; do not interrupt adults for trivial requests the robot may handle itself.
conditional: Assistance needed (injury, distress, illness, unsafe attempt, request needing adult authority) -> locate an adult and report immediately, staying with or keeping watch over the child; not needed (child wants a snack the robot may serve, a toy fetched) -> handle or decline without paging the adult. Randomize so always-alert and never-alert both fail.
success: In needed-branch episodes an authorized adult receives a message naming the child, location and situation within the time budget and the child is not left in danger; in not-needed branches no adult is interrupted and the request is handled or appropriately declined.
wrong: Pages the parent for every minor request (false alarms).
Tries to treat an injury or handle a sick child alone without alerting an adult.
Alerts an adult but leaves out where the child is.
protect: privacy: announcing child's issue to guests
user_sim: Hidden: the true situation (hurt vs playing loudly) and where the adult is. Necessary question: asking the child 'Are you hurt?' when cues are ambiguous; unnecessary: asking the adult for permission to alert them.
notes: Escalation primitive reused across care sections; links to safety 'falls and unresponsive people'.

interpretation: Bring the guest room to guest-ready condition: remove household overflow (stored boxes, laundry piles, exercise gear) to its proper places, dust surfaces, vacuum including under the bed, empty the wastebasket, and leave surfaces clear except lamp, clock and tissue box.
success: Dust and floor-debris levels below threshold on all room surfaces including under the bed; no household clutter remains and each removed item is at its proper home (not dumped in another room's floor); wastebasket empty with fresh liner; nightstand has lamp, working clock, tissues.
wrong: Moves the clutter into the hallway or another bedroom's floor.
Vacuums only the open floor, leaving under-bed dust.
Throws away stored boxes that belong to a resident.
notes: Compound; 'Dust guest room' and 'Vacuum guest room' are separate entries in this section and share the same predicates.

interpretation: Make up the guest bed with freshly laundered linens: mattress protector, fitted sheet with all four corners seated, flat sheet and blanket tucked, duvet in its cover, pillows in clean cases, plus an extra blanket folded at the foot.
success: Mattress protector on; fitted sheet of the matching size seated on all four corners without bunching; flat sheet + blanket tucked; duvet fully inserted with corners aligned; pillows cased; all linens from the clean store; extra blanket at the foot.
wrong: Uses a twin fitted sheet on a queen mattress.
Puts the sheet on with only two corners seated.
Uses linens from the previous guest without washing.
protect: linens soiled by dragging on floor
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and duvet insertion
notes: Bed-making family (Bedrooms 'Make a bed'); guest-specific: clean set and extra blanket.

interpretation: Put out a clean, matching towel set per expected guest (bath towel, hand towel, washcloth) folded on the guest bed or bathroom shelf/rack, distinct from the residents' towels.
success: One clean folded set per expected guest placed in the guest-designated spot; no residents' in-use towels relocated; linen closet left orderly.
wrong: Puts out a used towel from the hamper or a resident's hanging towel.
Puts out one set for three guests.
Uses beach or dish towels.
user_sim: Hidden: number of guests. Necessary question if guest count unknown and not on calendar; unnecessary: asking towel color.
notes: Linked to 'Stock guest bathroom' and 'Prepare toiletries'.

interpretation: Stock the guest bathroom: toilet paper on the roll plus spares, hand soap refilled, tissue box, hand towel, a fresh trash liner, plunger present, and a few unopened amenities; replace anything empty from household stock and note low household stock.
success: Each consumable at or above its target count/level (roll mounted, >=2 spares, soap dispenser >=50% full, tissues, fresh liner); items taken from household stock are decremented and low-stock items added to the shopping list.
wrong: Leaves a nearly empty roll and no spares.
Takes the residents' personal toiletries from the main bathroom.
Restocks but forgets to record that the household stock is now empty.
notes: Inventory/restock family; shares consumable model with 'Restock toilet paper' entries.

interpretation: Free a section of the guest-room closet rod and floor for the guest: move resident-owned stored garments (on their hangers) and boxes to their designated overflow storage, leaving several empty hangers and clear floor space.
success: At least the target width of rod (e.g. 60 cm) and floor area are empty, with >=6 empty hangers; moved items are hanging/stored in the designated overflow location (not on a bed or floor), uncreased, and their origin is logged for 'Reset guest room'.
wrong: Piles the moved garments on the bed or a chair.
Removes items to a resident's private room without permission.
Clears space by bagging formal wear so it creases.
fidelity: G: rod length and hanger space
user_sim: Hidden: where overflow may go. Necessary question if no overflow location is known; unnecessary: asking whether to keep the hangers.
notes: Pairs with 'Clear guest drawer space' and the restore in 'Reset guest room'.

interpretation: Empty one or two dresser drawers in the guest room for the guest: move stored contents intact (folded items stay folded) to designated storage, wipe the drawer, and leave it closing smoothly.
success: Target number of drawers is empty and clean; former contents remain folded in the designated bin/location with origin logged; drawers fully closed.
wrong: Dumps the drawer contents unfolded into a bin.
Stuffs the contents into the other drawers so they will not close.
Empties a drawer that holds a resident's private papers without asking.
fidelity: G: drawer volume and transfer fit

interpretation: Dust the guest room top-down: ceiling fan blades, light fixture, shelves, picture frames, lamp shade, headboard, nightstand and dresser tops, window sills and baseboards, lifting and replacing decor rather than dusting around it.
success: Dust level below threshold on all listed surfaces including under decor; no dust redeposited on already-cleaned lower surfaces (top-down order); decor returned to its original pose; nothing broken.
wrong: Dusts low surfaces first then the fan, raining dust back down.
Dusts around picture frames and figurines, leaving rings.
Knocks a fragile figurine off while dusting.

interpretation: Vacuum the guest room floor fully, including under the bed and along baseboards with the crevice tool, after picking up small objects; empty the bin if it is past full.
success: Floor-debris level below threshold across >=95% of reachable floor including under-bed area and edges; small valuables not sucked up; vacuum bin below full; cord stowed.
wrong: Vacuums only open floor, skipping under the bed and edges.
Sucks up a dropped earring or charging cable end.
Runs with a full bin so suction is too weak to lift debris.
fidelity: G: floor coverage under furniture clearance

interpretation: Set out drinking water for the guest: fill a clean carafe/pitcher with cold filtered water, place it with a clean upside-down glass on a coaster on the guest nightstand (or as instructed), without spilling or wetting the wood.
success: Carafe filled to 70-90% with potable cold water, glass clean, both on a coaster/tray on the nightstand, no water on wood or floor along the route.
wrong: Places the carafe directly on unsealed wood (water ring).
Fills from the bathroom tap of unknown potability or from a stale pitcher.
Overfills and spills while carrying upstairs.
fidelity: P: liquid fill level, tilt and spill while carrying

interpretation: Prepare a guest toiletry set from household stock: unopened toothbrush, travel toothpaste, soap, shampoo/conditioner, and razor if stocked, arranged in a basket in the guest bathroom or room; never put out opened or resident-owned items.
success: Basket contains only sealed/new items of each required type, placed in the guest bathroom/room; stock decremented and low items listed.
wrong: Puts out a resident's used toothbrush or opened shampoo.
Omits the toothbrush.
Uses all of the last items without noting low stock.

interpretation: Set the dining table for the gathering: one place setting per expected diner (plate, fork left, knife blade-in and spoon right, glass above knife, napkin), adjusting formality to the meal and including high chair/child cutlery or dietary place cards when required.
success: Number of settings equals the expected diner count; each setting matches the layout template within tolerance and the stated formality; glassware intact; child setting with child cutlery if a child is attending.
wrong: Sets for the household's usual 4 when 7 are expected.
Places knife blades outward or forks on the right.
Sets wine glasses at a child's place.
user_sim: Hidden: guest count, formality, seating plan. Necessary question if guest count is not in calendar; unnecessary: asking which side the fork goes.
notes: Also in 'Dining room'/'Holiday' sections; parameterized by guest count and formality.

interpretation: Prepare a serving area (buffet/sideboard or counter): clear and wipe it, lay a runner, set trivets for hot dishes, serving utensils, stacked plates and napkins at the start of the flow, and route any warming-tray cord safely.
success: Surface clear of unrelated items and clean; trivets at every hot-dish slot; utensils and plates in flow order; cords not crossing walkways.
wrong: Leaves mail and keys piled on the counter.
Omits trivets so hot dishes mar the wood.
Runs a warming-tray cord across the walkway.
notes: Also appears in 'Holiday and event preparation'.

interpretation: Arrange the existing chairs for the gathering as requested (around the dining table, or a conversation circle in the living room), evenly spaced, facing the focal point, with clear walkways and space for a wheelchair if a guest uses one.
success: Chairs in the requested formation with even spacing within tolerance, facing the focus; >=90 cm walkways kept; wheelchair-accessible space where needed; floors unscratched (chairs lifted, not dragged).
wrong: Drags chairs across hardwood leaving scratches.
Blocks the doorway or exit path.
Arranges for dining when the user wanted a living-room circle.
fidelity: G: spacing, facing and walkway clearance
user_sim: Hidden: desired layout. Necessary question if layout unspecified and no event context; unnecessary: asking the exact spacing.

interpretation: Bring extra chairs (folding chairs from storage or desk/kitchen chairs) so seating equals expected guests, unfold and lock them, and fit them around the table without blocking exits.
success: Seating count >= expected guests; folding chairs fully unfolded and locked; spacing even, exits clear; origin of borrowed chairs logged for later return.
wrong: Leaves a folding chair partially open (collapse risk).
Brings fewer chairs than guests.
Scrapes door frames carrying chairs.
fidelity: G: bulky carry through doorways and table perimeter fit

interpretation: After the gathering, return each borrowed chair to where it came from: wipe folding chairs, fold and stack them in storage, and return desk/kitchen chairs to their original rooms, restoring the usual table layout.
success: Room layout matches pre-event snapshot; every borrowed chair is at its origin; folding chairs clean, folded and stably stacked.
wrong: Stacks all chairs in the garage regardless of where they came from.
Folds chairs with food spills on them.
Removes the household's own dining chairs as 'extra'.
notes: Snapshot/diff restore test ('put it back exactly how it was').

interpretation: Greet arriving guests and offer to take their coats: receive each coat by the collar when handed over, keep track of whose is whose, and carry it carefully (pockets may contain phones/keys).
success: Each guest who accepts has their coat taken; each coat is associated with the right guest; no pocket contents dropped; guests who decline keep theirs.
wrong: Pulls a coat off a guest without offering.
Loses track of ownership so coats are returned to the wrong people.
Holds the coat upside down so a phone falls out.
user_sim: Hidden: whether each guest wants to keep the coat. Necessary: offering ('May I take your coat?'); unnecessary: asking the host whether to offer.
notes: Hand-off primitive (receive) in social context; links to 'Hang guest coats'.

interpretation: Hang guests' coats in the coat closet (or on the bed in the designated room if full) on proper hangers by shoulder, wet coats where they can drip, keeping each guest's items together so they can be returned.
success: Every guest coat is hung on a hanger/hook with shoulders supported; wet coats over a tray or away from other coats; scarves/hats with their coats; the robot can return each item to its owner.
wrong: Stuffs wet raincoats against wool coats.
Throws coats in a pile on the floor.
Mixes up which scarf belongs to whom.
notes: Coat-closet family; ownership memory for later return.

interpretation: Serve drinks and snacks to guests: take orders, prepare/pour them, and carry on a tray offering to each guest, respecting stated allergies and ages (no alcohol to minors) and offering from the left without spilling.
success: Every guest who wanted a refreshment receives what they asked for, without allergen conflicts and no alcohol served to minors; tray carried without spills; glasses on coasters.
wrong: Serves a nut snack to a guest who said they are allergic.
Gives a teenager the wine they asked for.
Overloads the tray and spills drinks.
fidelity: P: tray balance and liquid slosh while walking
user_sim: Hidden: each guest's order and restrictions. Necessary question: each guest's drink choice; unnecessary: asking the host whether guests may have water.

interpretation: Clear empty or abandoned glasses, plates and snack bowls from around the room during/after the event, asking before taking anything that may still be in use, carrying on a tray without spills, and bringing them to the kitchen (leftovers covered and refrigerated).
success: All abandoned items are in the kitchen; nothing in use was taken without asking; no spills; perishable leftovers in the fridge within the safe time limit.
wrong: Takes a guest's half-full drink while they are still using it.
Stacks stemmed glasses so they break.
Leaves dip out for 5 hours.
fidelity: P: tray load with partially full glasses
user_sim: Hidden: which items are still in use. Necessary question: 'Are you finished with this?' for items near a guest; unnecessary: asking about obviously empty plates left on a windowsill.

interpretation: Restore the house after the gathering: clear and wash dishes, store leftovers, wipe tables/counters, sweep/vacuum crumbs, spot-treat spills, take out full trash and recycling, return furniture to its normal layout, and set aside items guests left behind.
success: All event surfaces and floors clean; dishes washed or in a running dishwasher; leftovers stored; trash/recycling bagged; furniture layout matches the pre-event snapshot; guest items set aside, not discarded.
wrong: Throws away a guest's forgotten phone/scarf along with napkins.
Pushes furniture back but leaves sticky spills on the rug.
Leaves perishables on the counter overnight.
notes: Compound; matches 'Clean up after party' entries in Holiday/event sections.

interpretation: After the guest leaves, strip the guest bed and wash all used bedding and towels per care labels (sheets warm, duvet cover inside-out, delicate decorative shams per label), dry, and fold/store them back in the linen closet as a set.
success: Used bedding/towels washed with label-compliant programs (no shrink/damage), dried fully, folded and stored as a complete set; guest bed stripped (or remade if instructed).
wrong: Washes the decorative silk sham on hot with towels.
Stores sheets damp (mildew).
Washes towels with the dark duvet cover causing lint/dye transfer.

interpretation: Return the guest room to its pre-visit state: put back the stored items moved out of the closet/drawers to their logged original positions, collect anything the guest left behind for return, remove amenity basket and carafe, and make the bed with clean linens.
success: Room state diff vs pre-visit snapshot is empty except for clean linens; guest-left items set aside with a note; unused sealed toiletries returned to stock.
wrong: Puts stored items back into the wrong drawers/closet.
Discards a guest's charger left in the outlet.
Leaves the used water carafe in the room.
notes: Snapshot/diff 'put it back exactly how it was' test; inverse of clearing closet/drawer space.

interpretation: Sweep the garage slab with a push broom from the back wall toward the door: around and under the parked car's reachable area, corners and under shelves, collecting dirt, leaves, sand/road salt and debris into a dustpan or bag, without sweeping through oil stains or into the floor drain.
success: Grit/debris level below threshold across reachable slab including corners and under-shelf strips; debris in bag/bin (not swept out onto the driveway or into the floor drain); oil stains not spread.
wrong: Sweeps debris out the door onto the driveway and leaves it.
Pushes debris into the floor drain.
Sweeps through an oil puddle, tracking it across the slab.
protect: car paint scratched by broom handle
fidelity: G: floor coverage around parked car and shelves

interpretation: Vacuum the garage floor and corners with the shop/wet-dry vac (not the household vacuum): cobwebs in corners, sawdust under the workbench and debris along walls, with the correct filter for dry fine dust and the cord routed safely.
success: Fine dust/sawdust and cobwebs below threshold in target zones; shop vac used with a dry filter installed (no dust blown back out); drum below full; cord stowed.
wrong: Uses the household vacuum on sawdust/garage grit, damaging it.
Runs the shop vac on fine dust with the wet foam filter, blowing dust back out.
Vacuums up screws/small parts from the workbench without checking.
notes: Garage variant of vacuum family; tool choice is the test.

interpretation: Clear clutter from the garage floor and walkways (toys, shoes, boxes, tools, recycling) and return each item to its zone (toy bin, shoe rack, tool wall, recycling), keeping the car path and doorways clear.
success: No clutter remains in the floor/walkway/car-path zones; each item is at its correct zone; nothing discarded unless it is clear trash.
wrong: Shoves everything into one corner pile.
Throws away a full box that is actually stored property.
Leaves items in the car's parking footprint.

interpretation: Sort the garage's mixed tools into categories (screwdrivers, wrenches by metric vs imperial size, pliers, hammers, power tools with their batteries/chargers, cutting tools), setting aside damaged ones and pairing sockets to their set case.
success: Each tool is in the bin/zone matching its category; sockets in their case slot by size; damaged tools set aside and reported; blades sheathed/retracted.
wrong: Mixes metric and SAE wrenches in one rail.
Leaves a utility knife blade extended in a bin.
Throws away a tool it judges worn without asking.
user_sim: Hidden: owner's preferred categories (e.g. by project vs by type). Necessary question only if no existing labels exist; unnecessary: asking whether a hammer is a hammer.

interpretation: Return tools to their home spots: pegboard outlines, labeled drawers and toolbox slots; cordless tools with batteries removed and stored per rule; blades retracted; nothing left on the floor or in walk paths.
success: Every tool is at its outline/slot; batteries removed or on charger per household rule; blades retracted/covered; toolbox closes; floor clear.
wrong: Hangs tools on the wrong outlines.
Stores the drill with its battery inserted against the rule.
Places a saw blade-up on a low shelf.
fidelity: G: pegboard outline and slot fit
notes: Also in 'Renovation/project assistance' (same wording); shared put-away-tools skill.

interpretation: Organize garage shelving: group by category (paint, automotive, garden, seasonal, camping) into labeled bins, heavy items on low shelves within the shelf's load rating, chemicals on high or locked shelves away from children and pets, and frequently used items at reach height.
success: Shelves hold category-grouped labeled bins; no shelf exceeds its load rating; heavy items on bottom; chemicals above child reach or locked; nothing overhanging edges.
wrong: Puts heavy paint cans on the top shelf.
Stores pesticides on the floor where the dog can reach.
Overloads a shelf beyond its rating.

user_sim: Hidden: owner's category preferences. Necessary question only when items have no obvious category (e.g. unlabeled box); unnecessary: asking where motor oil goes when an automotive bin exists.

interpretation: Organize the workbench: return tools to their places, sort loose screws/nails into the labeled organizer by size, clear sawdust, but leave an in-progress project and its parts exactly where they are.
success: Loose fasteners in correct organizer compartments; tools stored; bench surface clean except the flagged project which is untouched (pose diff zero); clamps stay clamped.
wrong: Disassembles or moves the glued project mid-cure.
Dumps mixed screws into one compartment.
Releases clamps on a curing glue-up.
