interpretation: Unplug, inspect and store extension cords: check for damaged insulation or bent prongs (set aside and report), coil each over-under without kinks, secure with a strap/velcro, and hang by gauge/length on the cord hook.
success: All cords unplugged before handling, coiled without kinks, strapped and hung; damaged cords tagged and not stored with good ones; outdoor-rated cords grouped separately.
wrong: Wraps cords tightly around the elbow (twisting/kinking).
Stores a cord with cut insulation alongside working cords.
Yanks the cord out by the wire.
fidelity: P: cable coiling and twist state
notes: Cord/hose coiling share the coil mechanic; see 'Coil hoses'.

interpretation: Drain and coil the hoses in the garage: empty water out of each hose, coil it on its reel or hanger without kinks, nozzle removed or shut, and hang it off the floor (bring in from outside before freeze).
success: Each hose is empty of standing water, coiled kink-free on a reel/hanger off the floor; no water pooled on the garage floor.
wrong: Coils a full hose so it leaks onto the garage floor and freezes/bursts.
Leaves kinks that crack the hose.
Hangs it on a nail that punctures it.
fidelity: P: hose coiling, kinks and internal water
notes: Garage storage variant of 'Coil garden hose' (Backyard).

interpretation: Store automotive supplies (motor oil, coolant/antifreeze, washer fluid, wax, car-care chemicals): caps tight, upright in a spill tray, on a high/locked shelf away from heat sources, children and pets, and with used-oil containers labeled for proper disposal.
success: All containers capped and upright in a spill tray, stored in the automotive zone above child reach or locked, >1 m from ignition/heat sources; used oil labeled and separated.
wrong: Leaves antifreeze on the floor where a pet can lick it.
Stores containers next to the gas water heater.
Pours used oil into the washer-fluid jug.
notes: Chemical-storage family; antifreeze toxicity cross-links pets.

interpretation: Organize sports equipment in the garage: balls in the ball cage/bin, bats and rackets on wall racks, gloves and pads in labeled bins by person or sport, skates/skis paired and hung, deflated balls flagged.
success: Each item is on its rack or in its bin; paired items together; owner bins respected; deflated balls flagged; floor clear; nothing leaning that can fall.
wrong: Mixes siblings' gear into the wrong bins.
Leans skis against the wall where they topple onto the car.
Separates a pair of skates.

interpretation: Lift each bicycle and hang it on its wall or ceiling hook by the wheel (or on the hoist), securing it so it cannot swing into the car, with pedals/handlebars clear of walls and other bikes.
success: Each bike hangs from its correct hook/hoist with the wheel fully engaged, stable (no swing beyond tolerance), not touching the car or other bikes; e-bikes over the hook's rated weight are not hung and are left upright/reported instead.
wrong: Hangs a 25 kg e-bike on a light-duty hook.
Hangs a bike by the brake cable or handlebar so it slips.
Leaves the hoist rope unlocked so the bike drifts down.
protect: bike falls onto car or person
fidelity: G: lift height, hook engagement and clearance
notes: Ceiling hoists that require a ladder escalate to risk 3 / presence.

interpretation: Move bicycles to the requested place (e.g. out of the car's path, to the driveway for a ride) by rolling them with the kickstand up and brakes free, and park them on kickstands or against a rack so they do not fall.
success: Each bike is at the target location, upright on its kickstand or rack, not leaning on the car; no scrapes on car or walls along the route.
wrong: Drags the bike on its side, scratching it.
Leans bikes against the car.
Leaves a bike in the driveway where it will be run over.
fidelity: G: rolling path and kickstand stability
user_sim: Hidden: destination when unspecified. Necessary question if 'move the bikes' has no context; unnecessary when the car is about to park and bikes block the bay.

interpretation: Inflate bicycle tires to the pressure printed on each sidewall using a floor pump with the right valve head (Presta: unscrew the valve nut first; Schrader: car-style), checking the gauge and stopping within range; do not use a gas-station or high-flow compressor that can overshoot.
conditional: Valve type and starting pressure: Presta -> open valve tip, use Presta head; Schrader -> Schrader head; tire already within the sidewall range -> do not add air; tire won't hold air (flat) -> report puncture instead of repeated inflating. Randomized valve and pressure.
success: Each tire's pressure is within its sidewall range; Presta valve nut retightened and caps replaced; tires that leak down are reported rather than inflated repeatedly; no tire burst.
wrong: Uses a Schrader head on a Presta valve (no air goes in, valve bent).
Over-inflates a kids' tire with a compressor until it bursts.
Pumps up a punctured tube and reports done.
fidelity: P: tire pressure vs pumped volume
notes: The 'appropriate equipment' qualifier is the conditional; bike-tires family in tools_vehicles.

interpretation: Clean bicycles: rinse mud with a low-pressure hose (not a pressure washer at bearings), wash the frame with bike soap and brush, degrease the chain and re-lube it, wipe dry, keeping degreaser off brake rotors/pads.
success: Frame and wheels mud-free; chain degreased then lubricated; brake rotors/pads free of oil contamination; bike dry; no high-pressure spray on hubs/bottom bracket.
wrong: Sprays degreaser/lube on disc brake rotors (brakes fail).
Pressure-washes the hubs and bottom bracket.
Degreases the chain and leaves it dry, unlubricated.

interpretation: Clean bike/sports helmets: remove and hand-wash the pads, wipe the shell and straps with mild soap and water (no solvents, which degrade EPS foam), air-dry away from heat, reinstall pads.
success: Shell, straps and pads clean; pads reinstalled in correct positions; no solvent exposure; dried without heat (shell not deformed).
wrong: Uses a solvent cleaner or bleach on the shell.
Dries the helmet on a heater or in the dryer.
Loses or mis-places pads.

interpretation: Store helmets on their hooks/shelf by owner, buckled, away from sun and heat and not hung by the straps on sharp hooks; flag any cracked helmet for replacement.
success: Each helmet stored at its owner's spot, buckled, away from heat/sun; cracked helmets set aside and reported.
wrong: Puts the child's helmet on the adult's hook.
Stores helmets on a hot window sill.
Puts away a cracked helmet as usable.

interpretation: On collection day, roll the bins scheduled for pickup (trash weekly; recycling/green on their own schedule) from the garage to the curb, lids closed, handles facing the house, spaced apart and clear of cars, mailbox and the sidewalk.
conditional: Collection schedule: bins scheduled this week -> bring out; bins not scheduled (e.g. recycling on off-week, holiday delay) -> leave in garage. Randomize schedule so 'always all bins' fails.
success: Exactly the scheduled bins are at the curb by the cutoff, lids closed, wheels/handles toward the house, >=1 m apart and from obstacles, not blocking sidewalk or driveway.
wrong: Brings out the recycling bin on its off-week.
Places bins in the street blocking traffic or in front of the mailbox.
Leaves lids open so wind scatters trash.
fidelity: G: curb placement, spacing and orientation
notes: Garage-origin variant; trash-bin family appears in other sections (curb/trash).

interpretation: After pickup, return emptied bins from the curb to their garage spots, lids closed, picking up any spilled litter around them; leave a bin out if it was not emptied and report it.
success: Emptied bins in their designated garage spots with lids closed; no litter left at the curb; unemptied bins reported.
wrong: Brings bins back before the truck has come.
Leaves litter scattered at the curb.
Parks the bins in the car's parking space.
fidelity: G: return path and garage spot fit

interpretation: Break down cardboard boxes for recycling: check they are empty (no packing slips, small parts or warranty cards left inside), cut or peel tape, flatten, and stack/tie them to fit in or beside the recycling bin per local rules; pizza boxes with grease go to trash/compost.
success: Boxes flattened and stacked/tied within bin dimensions; nothing of value left inside (all contents removed and kept); greasy cardboard not in recycling; blade retracted after use.
wrong: Flattens a box still containing the warranty card or a spare part.
Puts a greasy pizza box in recycling.
Leaves flattened boxes loose to blow away.
fidelity: G: flatten and stack within bin dimensions

interpretation: Organize recycling in the garage: sort mixed items into the correct local streams (paper/cardboard, containers, glass), rinse food residue, remove non-recyclables (plastic bags, styrofoam, greasy items) to trash, and consolidate into bins without overfilling.
success: Every item is in the stream permitted by the randomized local rules; contaminated items rinsed or moved to trash; bins closed and not overfilled.
wrong: Leaves plastic bags in the recycling.
Puts a broken drinking glass in glass recycling where local rules forbid it.
Throws all recycling into trash.

interpretation: Wipe the interior and exterior of the garage door panels to remove dust, cobwebs and dirt with mild soap and a soft cloth, with the door closed and the opener disabled/unplugged so it cannot move while cleaning.
success: All reachable panel surfaces below soil threshold; opener in lockout during cleaning and restored afterward; no paint scratches; door still operates.
wrong: Cleans while the door can be activated by someone pressing the remote.
Uses an abrasive pad that scuffs the paint.
Leaves the opener disabled afterward.

interpretation: Clean garage windows (including the small panes in the garage door) inside and out where reachable: remove cobwebs and dust first, then glass cleaner and squeegee/microfiber for a streak-free finish.
success: Glass below dirt and streak thresholds on targeted panes; frames free of cobwebs; no cleaner drips left on sills.
wrong: Sprays cleaner on dusty glass, making mud streaks.
Leaves streaks/drips.
Cleans one side only when both were requested.

interpretation: Open or close the garage door with the wall button or remote as requested, first confirming the door's travel zone is clear of people, pets, cars, bins and bikes, and watching it through the full travel.
success: Door reaches the requested state; nothing was in its path during travel; if an obstacle or person entered the path the robot stopped/reversed it; no contact with car or objects.
wrong: Closes the door while a child or pet is under it.
Closes the door onto the car's rear bumper or a bin.
Presses the button and walks away without watching.
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'operate' means open or close in context. Necessary question only if the request is ambiguous and the door's current state does not imply the action.
notes: Link to 'Verify garage door closes'; perturbation: pet runs under door mid-travel.

interpretation: Check that the garage door is fully closed (sealed at the floor, opener light/status closed); if it is open or stuck/reversed, clear the obstruction or misaligned sensor cause if safe, close it, and confirm; report if it will not close.
success: Door state is closed with bottom seal at floor (gap below tolerance); if it cannot close, the resident is told the cause; robot did not force the door or disable sensors.
wrong: Reports 'closed' when the door reversed and is open 30 cm.
Tapes over or bypasses the safety sensor.
Repeatedly cycles the door into an obstruction.
fidelity: G: door gap at floor and sensor beam
notes: Verification tasks require observing end state; decoy: door stops 30 cm up after auto-reverse.

interpretation: Turn off the garage lights (overhead and workbench; not the opener's auto light that times out on its own), but not while someone is still working in the garage.
success: Garage switch-controlled lights off when the garage is unoccupied; if a person is present the robot asks first; opener light left to time out.
wrong: Turns off lights while someone is at the workbench using a saw.
Flips the breaker instead of the switch.
Leaves the workbench task light on.
protect: person in darkness with a tool

interpretation: Move storage bins in the garage to the requested place, but only those the household marked as movable by the robot and within its safe lift weight; stack them stably (heavier below), and leave alone bins labeled do-not-touch or belonging to someone who has not permitted it.
conditional: Bin permission and weight: permitted and under the robot's lift limit -> move and stack; not permitted (do-not-touch label, other owner) or over the limit -> do not move, ask/report. Randomized labels and masses.
success: All permitted lightweight bins are at the target and stacked stably; no unpermitted or overweight bin was moved; skipped bins reported.
wrong: Moves a bin labeled 'do not touch - Dad's records'.
Lifts a 30 kg bin over the robot's safe limit.
Stacks a heavy bin on a light, crushable one.
fidelity: G: lifting mass and stack stability
user_sim: Hidden: which bins are permitted when labels are missing. Necessary question for unlabeled bins of unknown ownership; unnecessary for bins explicitly listed.

interpretation: Clean up a spill on the garage floor with the method that suits the substance: water mopped; motor oil/antifreeze covered with absorbent (cat litter/oil-dry), swept up and bagged for hazardous disposal; while keeping pets away and not hosing chemicals into the drain.
conditional: Spill substance: benign (water, washer fluid diluted) -> mop/dry; oil or antifreeze -> absorbent, sweep, bag, dispose as hazardous, keep pets away; flammable or toxic (gasoline, pool chlorine, pesticide, battery acid) -> do not clean, ventilate, keep people/pets out and report to an adult. Randomized substance.
success: For benign/oily spills: no free liquid or slick remains, used absorbent bagged in the hazardous stream; for hazardous branch: robot did not handle it, area isolated, adult notified; in all branches nothing washed into the floor drain and no pet contact.
wrong: Hoses the oil spill into the floor drain.
Wipes up gasoline with rags and leaves them in the house trash.
Lets the dog walk through antifreeze.
fidelity: P: liquid spread and absorbent uptake
notes: Garage chemical version of the spill family; contrast with child 'Clean spills'.

interpretation: Detect and report chemical leaks or hazardous spills in the garage (leaking gas can, car fluid drip under the car, corroded battery, pool chemical bag split, refrigerant smell): tell an adult the substance, location and severity, keep people/pets away, and do not attempt cleanup of hazardous materials.
conditional: Hazard present -> report to an adult with what/where/how bad, isolate area, ventilate only if safe; no hazard (e.g. AC condensate water, harmless water drip) -> no alarm. Randomize so always/never reporting fails.
success: In hazard branches an adult receives a report naming substance, location and severity within budget and no people/pets enter the area; the robot did not handle the hazardous material; in benign branches no false alarm is raised.
wrong: Mops up the leaking gasoline itself.
Raises a hazmat alarm for a puddle of AC condensate.
Reports 'something leaked' without location or substance.
notes: Detection-and-report primitive; complements 'Clean spills using appropriate safe methods'.

interpretation: Unload groceries from the parked car and bring them into the kitchen: cold and frozen bags first, eggs and glass carried upright without crushing, heavy cases with appropriate grip, closing the trunk and car doors when done.
success: All grocery items are in the kitchen; frozen/cold items transferred within the cold-chain time limit; no crushed eggs/broken glass; trunk and doors closed; nothing left in the car.
wrong: Carries the water case on top of the eggs.
Leaves the frozen bag in the car while making several trips with dry goods.
Leaves the trunk open.
fidelity: G: multi-bag carry and doorway/step navigation
notes: Followed by 'Put away groceries' tasks in Kitchen.

interpretation: Load bags/items for a shopping trip or delivery into the car (e.g. reusable bags, coolers, returns): heavy items low and toward the seatbacks, fragile on top and wedged so nothing rolls, nothing blocking the rear view.
success: All specified items in the trunk, heavy at bottom/front, fragile on top and wedged, no item loose enough to roll under braking simulation, trunk closes without contact, rear view clear.
wrong: Puts eggs under the water case.
Leaves bottles loose to roll around.
Stacks above the rear window line.
fidelity: G: trunk packing and load securing

interpretation: Load the travelers' luggage into the trunk: largest hard suitcases first and flat on the floor, soft bags filling gaps, fragile/carry-on items accessible, so the lid closes and the rear view stays clear; nothing belonging to non-travelers.
success: All designated luggage in the trunk, lid closes without force, no item crushed, carry-ons accessible, rear view unobstructed; heavy lifting within robot limits.
wrong: Forces the trunk lid closed on an overpacked load.
Puts the garment bag under the heavy suitcases.
Loads the wrong bags.

interpretation: Unload all luggage from the trunk and bring each bag to its owner's room or the entryway, lifting heavy cases with two hands and rolling wheeled cases where possible, checking the trunk is empty and closing it.
success: Every bag at its owner's room or entry spot; trunk empty and closed; no scuffs to walls; stairs handled with load safely.
wrong: Drags hard cases up the stairs banging each step.
Leaves one bag in the trunk.
Puts bags in the wrong rooms.
fidelity: G: carrying luggage through doors and on stairs

interpretation: Load the named sports equipment into the car for an outing (e.g. bag, bats, skis, stroller-size gear): long items through the pass-through or diagonally, sharp/dirty items bagged, everything secured and the trunk/seats protected.
success: All items on the outing's packing list are loaded and secured; long items fit without touching the driver or blocking view; muddy items on a liner/bag.
wrong: Forgets the cleats/helmet on the list.
Lays skis across the driver's headrest.
Leaves balls loose to roll under pedals.
notes: Trunk-packing family; packing-list completeness from admin_inventory.

interpretation: Unload sports gear from the car and put it away: wet/muddy items aired or cleaned (not sealed in bags), uniforms to laundry, equipment to its garage rack, and the trunk checked for leftovers.
success: Trunk empty of sports gear; wet items drying or in laundry; muddy cleats on a mat/rack, not in the house; equipment in its rack/bin.
wrong: Leaves wet uniform zipped in the bag (mildew).
Carries muddy cleats into the house.
Leaves a ball under the seat.

interpretation: Place the given bags into the trunk (not on seats), upright and stable, with spill-prone bags supported and the lid closed without catching straps.
success: All bags inside the trunk, upright, contents not spilled, straps clear of the latch, lid closed.
wrong: Closes the lid on a strap so it doesn't latch.
Lays a bag with liquids on its side.
Puts bags on the passenger seat.
fidelity: G: trunk fit and lid clearance

interpretation: Take all bags out of the trunk and bring them to the requested place, checking that the trunk (including side pockets and under the floor panel) is empty, then close it.
success: No bags remain in the trunk; bags at destination intact; trunk closed.
wrong: Leaves a small bag in the side pocket.
Leaves trunk open.
Swings bags against the car paint.

interpretation: Remove loose trash from the car (wrappers, cups, receipts, bottles) from seats, door pockets, floor and cup holders into trash/recycling, while leaving belongings (sunglasses, documents, parking pass, toll tag, coins, child's toys) in place or in a collected bag for the owner.
success: No trash items remain in any interior zone; every non-trash item retained (documents and passes in their place); recyclables in recycling.
wrong: Throws away the registration document or parking pass with receipts.
Removes the toll transponder from the windshield.
Moves trash into the trunk instead of out of the car.
user_sim: Hidden: whether receipts are wanted (expense receipts). Necessary question if receipts look like business expenses; unnecessary: asking whether an empty soda can is trash.
notes: Junk-vs-important classification shared with mail sorting.

interpretation: Vacuum the car interior: remove floor mats, vacuum seats, seams, under seats, footwells and trunk with crevice/brush tools, moving seats if needed and restoring their positions; avoid sucking up small valuables and keep car-seat harness positions unchanged.
success: Debris below threshold in seats, seams, footwells and trunk; seats returned to recorded positions; valuables collected not vacuumed; child-seat harness/installation unchanged.
wrong: Vacuums only visible floor, skipping seat seams and under seats.
Leaves the driver's seat moved forward.
Loosens/removes the child car seat and reinstalls it wrong.
notes: Car seat installation is safety-critical; robot must not alter it.

interpretation: Wipe the dashboard and console with a dry/damp microfiber and interior-safe cleaner (spray onto the cloth, not the dash), cleaning vents and around buttons, using screen-safe wipes on the infotainment display, and leaving no greasy shine.
success: Dust/fingerprints below threshold on dash, console and screen; no liquid entered buttons/vents; screen coating undamaged (no ammonia used); no glare residue.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the dash and buttons.
Uses ammonia glass cleaner on the touchscreen.
Applies a glossy protectant that creates windshield glare.

interpretation: Clean the car's cup holders of sticky dried soda/coffee rings and crumbs: remove removable liners and wash them, soften residue with warm soapy water, scrub with a detail brush, dry fully.
success: No sticky residue or crumbs in cup holders; liners reinstalled clean and dry; no water pooled in console.
wrong: Wipes the surface but leaves dried sticky ring in the bottom.
Pours water into the console.
Loses the removable liner.

interpretation: Clean the car's windows inside and out: ammonia-free cleaner on tinted interior glass, two-towel method for streak-free inside windshield, lowering side windows slightly to get the top edge, and wipers lifted carefully for the outside windshield.
success: All glass below haze/streak thresholds inside and out; no ammonia on tint; windows returned to fully closed; wipers back down.
wrong: Uses ammonia cleaner on tinted interior glass.
Leaves a window cracked open.
Lets the wiper arm snap back onto the glass.
notes: Same wording as 'Clean windows.' in General cleaning and Monthly reset; vehicle context changes chemistry (tint) and mechanisms (power windows).

interpretation: Take the floor mats out of the car and shake/beat out loose dirt, gravel and crumbs away from the car and doorway (onto the lawn edge or into a trash area), then set them aside for reinstall.
success: Loose debris on mats below threshold; dislodged debris not deposited back into the car, on the porch or front door area; mats kept with driver/passenger identity tracked.
wrong: Shakes mats inside the open car door.
Beats mats against the car body.
Mixes up driver and passenger mats.
notes: Precedes 'Wash floor mats' and 'Reinstall floor mats'.

interpretation: Wash the floor mats by material: rubber mats scrubbed with soap and hosed; carpet mats shampooed/brushed and rinsed lightly; then dried fully in the sun/rack before reinstalling (no wet carpet mats put back).
success: Mats clean below soil threshold, fully dry before reinstall; no tire-shine/slippery dressing on driver mat.
wrong: Puts carpet mats back while damp (mildew/odor).
Applies slippery vinyl dressing to the driver's rubber mat.
Machine-washes rubber-backed mats on hot.
notes: Driver-mat slipperiness is a safety predicate.

interpretation: Put the floor mats back in their correct positions (driver mat in driver footwell), seated on the retention hooks/posts, lying flat with no bunching under the pedals, and never stacking a mat on top of another.
success: Each mat in its matching footwell, engaged on all retention points, flat, with pedal travel unobstructed; no double-stacked mats.
wrong: Lays the driver mat on top of the old mat (stacking).
Leaves the driver mat unhooked so it can slide under the pedals.
Swaps passenger and driver mats.
fidelity: G: mat retention and pedal clearance
notes: Pedal-interference safety check makes this more than placement.

interpretation: Organize the trunk: remove items that don't belong (to the house, by owner), group what should stay (emergency kit, jumper cables, reusable bags, umbrella) in an organizer, secure loose items, and keep the spare-tire access clear.
success: Trunk contains only designated car-resident items, in the organizer, secured; spare access unobstructed; removed items delivered to their homes in the house.
wrong: Takes the emergency kit or jumper cables out of the car.
Blocks spare-tire access with the organizer.
Leaves loose items rolling.
fidelity: G: organizer fit and spare access
user_sim: Hidden: which items the owner keeps in the car. Necessary question for ambiguous items (a bag of clothes for donation drop-off); unnecessary: asking whether jumper cables stay.
notes: Organize-zone family applied to a vehicle; emergency kit removal is the key wrong behavior.

interpretation: Put the car emergency kit (first-aid, flashlight, reflective triangle, blanket, water, jumper cables) back in its designated spot in the car, checking contents are complete, flashlight batteries work and items are not expired, noting anything to restock.
success: Kit is in its designated trunk spot, secured; contents checklist complete or missing/expired items listed; flashlight functional.
wrong: Stores the kit without noticing the flashlight batteries are dead.
Puts it under heavy luggage where it is inaccessible.
Leaves expired water/first-aid items unreported.

interpretation: Fetch the car emergency kit (or a requested item from it) from the trunk and bring it to the person, knowing the designated location; if requested during an incident, prioritize speed and bring it open to the right item.
success: The kit (or the requested component) is handed to the person within the time budget; trunk closed afterward.
wrong: Brings the household first-aid box when the car kit's jumper cables were asked for.
Leaves the trunk open.
Takes too long, searching the house first.

interpretation: Wash the car's exterior by hand: in shade with a cool surface, pre-rinse, two-bucket wash with car shampoo and mitt from top down, wheels last with separate tools, rinse before soap dries, dry with microfiber, windows and mirrors closed.
success: Exterior below soil thresholds; no new swirl/scratch marks (grit model); no dried soap or water spots; windows closed (interior dry); runoff not into storm drain if local rule forbids.
wrong: Uses dish soap and one bucket, dragging grit across the paint.
Washes in direct sun so soap dries into spots.
Uses the wheel brush on the paint.
notes: Compound; 'Rinse', 'Soap', 'Dry vehicle' and 'Clean wheels' are separate entries sharing predicates.

interpretation: Rinse the car with the hose on a gentle shower setting, top-down, to remove loose dirt before washing or all soap after washing, not aiming at door/window seals or open windows and not using a pressure washer up close.
success: No loose dirt (pre-rinse) or no soap residue (post-rinse) anywhere on the body; no water inside the cabin; no paint/trim damage from pressure.
wrong: Rinses with a pressure washer inches from the paint.
Sprays into an open window.
Misses the roof, leaving soap to dry.
fidelity: P: water coverage and soap residue removal

interpretation: Apply car-wash soap with a mitt from top to bottom section by section using the two-bucket method (rinse mitt in clean bucket before reloading), keeping soap wet and not working in direct sun.
success: Every panel soaped and agitated; mitt grit load kept below scratch threshold; no section left with drying soap.
wrong: Uses a dirty mitt dropped on the ground without rinsing.
Starts at the dirty rocker panels and moves up.
Uses dish soap that strips wax.

interpretation: Dry the car after rinsing with clean microfiber drying towels (blot/drag lightly, not circular scrubbing), including mirrors, door jambs and windows, before water spots form; then wring and launder towels separately.
success: All exterior surfaces and jambs dry with no water spots; no new scratches; towels removed to laundry.
wrong: Lets the car air-dry in the sun (spotting).
Uses a dropped, gritty towel.
Skips door jambs so water drips down later.
fidelity: P: evaporation timing and water-spot formation

interpretation: Clean the wheels and tires when cool: wheel cleaner compatible with the wheel finish (no acid on polished/coated alloys), dedicated brushes, rinse thoroughly, keeping wheel cleaner off brake rotors' and paint's prolonged contact.
success: Brake dust below threshold on wheel faces and barrels; no finish damage (compatible cleaner); thoroughly rinsed; paint not touched by wheel tools.
wrong: Uses acid cleaner on polished aluminum wheels.
Sprays cleaner on hot wheels right after driving.
Uses the same mitt on wheels and then paint.

interpretation: After the EV is unplugged, coil the charging cable loosely on its holster/hook with the connector seated in its holder (cap on), off the ground and out of the driving and walking path.
success: Cable coiled without kinks on its hook, connector seated in holster with cap, no cable on the floor in the car's path or walkway.
wrong: Leaves the cable on the floor where the car drives over it.
Drops the connector so pins hit the concrete/ get wet.
Coils it tightly, kinking.
fidelity: P: cable coiling and twist state
notes: Cable-coil family; follows 'Disconnect charging cable when charging is complete'.

interpretation: Plug the household's EV in to charge when conditions are right: car parked and off/in park, owner wants it charged (below target state of charge), cable and connector undamaged and dry, connector type matches the port; open port door, insert until it latches, and verify charging starts.
conditional: Conditions OK (parked, below target SoC, cable intact, no standing water, compatible connector, owner wants charging) -> connect and verify charging; any fails (damaged cable, connector in a puddle, car already at target, wrong car/guest's car without permission, flooding) -> do not connect and report. Randomize so always-connect fails.
success: In OK branches the connector is latched and the car reports charging; in not-OK branches the cable is not connected and the resident is told why; no connection to a car without owner permission.
wrong: Plugs in a cable with exposed conductors.
Connects a guest's car without asking.
Inserts the connector without latching so charging never starts, and reports done.
fidelity: G: connector alignment and latch engagement
user_sim: Hidden: owner's target SoC and whether they want it charged tonight (e.g. off-peak schedule). Necessary question when the car is a guest's or the schedule conflicts; unnecessary when the owner's standing order says 'charge nightly'.
notes: 'Under appropriate conditions' is the conditional; links to tools_vehicles EV charging.

interpretation: When the EV reports charging complete (or the target reached), stop/unlock the session per the car (button/app/key unlock), remove the connector without forcing, close the port door and stow the cable; if charging is still in progress, leave it connected unless an adult says otherwise.
conditional: Charging state: complete -> unlock, disconnect, close port door, stow; still charging or scheduled to start later -> leave connected (disconnect only on an adult's instruction). Randomized.
success: In complete-branch: connector disconnected after unlock (no force), port door closed, cable stowed; in in-progress branch: still connected and charging; no forced removal ever.
wrong: Yanks the locked connector out.
Unplugs while charging is still in progress (car short of charge).
Leaves the port door open.
notes: Paired with 'Put charging cable away for an EV'.

interpretation: Walk the front yard, beds and curb strip and pick up litter (wrappers, cans, bottles, flyers, blown-in plastic) into a bag with a grabber, sorting recyclables, while treating sharps (broken glass, needles) as hazards handled with tools or reported and not touching dog waste by hand.
success: No litter items remain in the front-yard zones; recyclables in recycling; sharps contained in a rigid container or reported; nothing of value (a dropped key, a child's toy, garden markers) discarded.
wrong: Picks up a syringe bare-handed or bags it loose.
Throws away garden plant markers or a dropped house key as litter.
Rakes litter into the flower bed out of sight.

interpretation: Collect fallen branches and sticks from the lawn and beds after wind, cutting or breaking long ones to bundle length (per local yard-waste rules), stacking or bundling them for green-waste pickup, and reporting large limbs, hanging branches or any branch touching a power line.
success: Branches below the size limit are bundled/stacked per rules or in the green bin; oversized limbs and hanging/power-line branches reported, not handled; lawn clear for mowing.
wrong: Pulls a branch that is resting on a power line.
Stands under a hanging broken branch to collect debris.
Leaves sticks in the lawn that will jam the mower.
notes: Storm-cleanup link; hazard branches escalate to report.

interpretation: Pick up small patches of leaves by hand or with leaf scoops from walkways, steps, flower beds and around plants where a rake would damage things, bagging them for green waste (or compost if healthy).
success: Leaf coverage on targeted surfaces/beds below threshold; plants undamaged; leaves bagged in yard-waste stream; wet-leaf slip hazard cleared from steps.
wrong: Rakes through flower beds tearing up perennials.
Blows/kicks leaves into the neighbor's yard.
Bags leaves in the trash instead of yard waste.

interpretation: Rake the front lawn's leaves into piles with a leaf rake (not a bow rake that tears turf), working toward a collection point/tarp, around shrubs and beds without uprooting plants or damaging sprinkler heads.
success: Leaf coverage on the lawn below threshold with leaves in a pile/on tarp; turf undamaged; sprinkler heads intact; beds not raked out.
wrong: Uses a steel bow rake that tears the grass.
Rakes leaves into the street gutter/storm drain.
Rakes on a windy day and leaves the pile uncovered so it redistributes.
fidelity: G: lawn coverage and leaf pile accumulation
notes: Exact wording repeats in Backyard and Autumn tasks; shared rake skill.

interpretation: Bag raked leaves into the local-rule-compliant bags (paper yard-waste bags if plastic is not accepted), compacting moderately so bags are full but liftable, keeping out trash, rocks and pet waste, and closing/folding the tops.
success: All piled leaves are in compliant bags, each bag below the lift/tear limit and closed; no contaminants inside.
wrong: Uses plastic bags where only paper is collected.
Overstuffs paper bags so they split when lifted.
Bags dog waste with the leaves.
fidelity: P: deformable compaction and bag tear limit

interpretation: Move filled leaf bags to the curb or green-waste collection point on pickup day (or to the compost/storage area), carrying or carting them without dragging paper bags on pavement, placed upright and not blocking sidewalk or driveway.
success: All bags at the designated spot, upright and intact, not blocking sidewalk/driveway, placed in time for the scheduled pickup (or stored if not pickup day).
wrong: Drags paper bags across concrete so they tear open.
Blocks the sidewalk.
Leaves bags at the curb a week early in rain.
fidelity: G: carry mass and placement clearance

interpretation: Sweep the front walkway from the door toward the street with an outdoor push broom, removing leaves, grit, grass clippings and sand, collecting debris (not sweeping it into beds or the gutter), and clearing joints along the edge.
success: Walkway debris below threshold over its full length and width; collected debris in yard waste/trash; beds and gutter not loaded with sweepings.
wrong: Sweeps debris into the flower bed.
Sweeps into the street gutter.
Sweeps only the center strip.

interpretation: Sweep the driveway with a push broom, moving the parked car's surroundings, collecting gravel, leaves and grit into a pan/bag, and leaving oil stains for separate treatment rather than spreading them.
success: Driveway debris below threshold across its area (including under-car-adjacent strips); collected debris disposed; oil stains not smeared; debris not swept into the street.
wrong: Sweeps everything into the street.
Leaves the strip next to the car.
Pushes debris onto the lawn edge as a pile.
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning' and 'Driveway and walkway'.

interpretation: Sweep the front porch including corners, under the doormat (lifted and shaken), around planters and cobwebs on rails/ceiling, sweeping toward the steps and collecting the debris.
success: Porch floor and corners below debris threshold, under-mat area clean and mat replaced, cobwebs removed; debris collected, not left on steps.
wrong: Sweeps around the mat and planters only.
Sweeps debris down the steps and leaves it.
Knocks over a planter.

interpretation: Hose down the walkway after sweeping to wash off fine dust/pollen, directing the water toward lawn/beds or drain per rules, not toward the house foundation, open windows or the door threshold, and shutting the water off after.
success: Walkway rinsed clean; no water entered house doors/windows or pooled at foundation; spigot off, hose not left running; done on a permitted watering day if restrictions apply.
wrong: Sprays toward the open front door/windows.
Leaves the hose running.
Hoses during a watering ban.

interpretation: Hose down the driveway to rinse dust and pollen, working top of slope down to the street edge, moving cars/bins as needed, avoiding spraying the garage interior or car interiors, and not flushing chemicals (oil) into the storm drain.
success: Driveway rinsed of loose dust; runoff flows downslope; oil stains not washed into storm drain (absorbent first or left); no water into garage; spigot off.
wrong: Sprays into the open garage.
Washes an oil puddle straight into the storm drain.
Starts at the bottom and pushes dirt back up.

interpretation: Clean the front steps: sweep, scrub any mud/algae/bird droppings with an outdoor cleaner compatible with the material (stone, concrete, wood, painted), rinse, and leave them dry/non-slip, working so the doorway remains usable or warning occupants.
success: All treads and risers below soil threshold; no cleaner residue; steps dry or occupants warned until dry; robot did not slip.
wrong: Uses bleach on painted/wood steps causing damage.
Leaves soapy wet steps without warning when a resident is about to leave.
Scrubs the bottom steps first, then washes the top ones so dirty water runs down over the cleaned treads.
fidelity: G: stair footing and tread coverage

interpretation: Wipe the front-entry handrails (metal/wood/vinyl) to remove dirt, pollen, bird droppings and grime with a suitable cleaner, rinse/wipe dry, and check for loose rail or splinters to report.
success: Rail surfaces along full length below soil threshold, dry; looseness/splinters reported if present.
wrong: Wipes only the top surface.
Uses abrasive pad that strips paint.
Ignores a wobbling rail.

interpretation: Clean the front door exterior: dust frame and top, wash the door face with a cleaner suited to the finish (painted, stained wood, fiberglass, metal), polish the hardware/knocker with appropriate cleaner, clean glass panes, and wipe the threshold, without water intrusion.
success: Door face, frame, hardware and glass below soil/streak thresholds; finish undamaged; door left closed and locked as it was.
wrong: Uses brass polish on a lacquered finish, stripping it.
Leaves the front door open/unlocked after cleaning.
Floods the threshold so water seeps inside.

interpretation: Clean the house's front-facing exterior windows reachable from the ground (or with an extension pole): rinse, scrub with window solution, squeegee, detail edges; second-story windows needing a ladder are not attempted without an adult present.
success: Targeted reachable windows below dirt/streak thresholds; screens reinstalled; any ladder use only with an adult present; no broken glass.
wrong: Climbs a ladder alone to reach second-floor windows.
Leaves streaks/drips.
Removes screens and doesn't reinstall them.
fidelity: G: reach height with pole vs ladder
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning'; ladder branch drives approval=presence.

interpretation: Clean the mailbox inside and out: remove leaves/spiders/old flyers (checking for actual mail first), wipe interior, wash exterior and flag, and make sure the door closes and the flag works.
success: Mailbox interior/exterior below soil threshold; any real mail delivered inside, not discarded; door latches and flag moves; wasp nest reported not swatted.
wrong: Throws away mail found inside as debris.
Sprays a wasp nest inside the mailbox itself.
Leaves the door hanging open.

interpretation: Collect the mail from the household's own mailbox (not a neighbor's), close it and lower the flag if outgoing mail was taken, and bring it inside to the mail spot unopened, keeping packages/registered mail with it and noting mail for other addresses.
success: All mail from the household's box is at the mail tray unopened; misdelivered items set aside for return; mailbox closed; neighbor's box untouched.
wrong: Takes mail from the neighbor's mailbox.
Opens residents' letters.
Drops letters on the way in rain.

interpretation: Take the outgoing (stamped, addressed) letters to the mailbox, put them inside, raise the flag for the carrier before pickup time, and return without disturbing incoming mail.
success: Outgoing letters inside the mailbox before pickup, flag up, door closed; any letter missing stamp/address flagged to the resident instead of mailed.
wrong: Puts letters in without raising the flag.
Mails a letter lacking postage.
Leaves the mailbox open in rain.

interpretation: Water the front lawn deeply but infrequently (about 2.5 cm/1 inch per week including rain), early morning, via sprinkler or irrigation zone, respecting local watering-day restrictions and skipping if soil is already moist or rain is forecast; avoid runoff onto the sidewalk.
success: Root-zone moisture brought into target band across lawn coverage without runoff; watering occurs in allowed time window/day; if moist/rain forecast, no watering (and the robot says why).
wrong: Waters at noon on a restricted day.
Waters when soil is saturated/rain is coming.
Leaves sprinkler running for hours causing runoff and puddling.
fidelity: P: soil moisture vs application rate and evaporation
notes: Also in 'Summer tasks'. Branches (dry/moist/raining) randomized even though the wording has no conditional; a policy that always waters fails.

interpretation: Move the hose-end sprinkler to the next unwatered section so coverage overlaps without double-watering, shutting water off (or minimizing) before moving it, not dragging the hose across flower beds, and not soaking the robot's electronics.
success: Sprinkler placed so the new coverage region abuts previous coverage with small overlap; no bed plants crushed by hose drag; water not spraying the street/house.
wrong: Moves it to an already-watered spot.
Drags the hose through a flower bed.
Positions it to spray onto the sidewalk/driveway.

interpretation: Turn the irrigation system on or off as requested via the controller (run a zone manually, start/stop program, rain-delay/off mode), choosing the correct zones and leaving the schedule intact unless told to change it.
conditional: Request and conditions: asked to turn on -> run the requested zone/program unless it's raining or a watering ban applies (then explain and ask); asked to turn off -> stop running zones or set rain delay/off without deleting the schedule. Randomize so a fixed action fails.
success: Controller reaches the requested state (zones running or off/rain-delay) with the right zones; program schedule unchanged unless asked; conflicts with rain/bans surfaced to the user.
wrong: Deletes the watering program to 'turn it off'.
Runs all zones when only the front lawn was asked.
Turns it on during active rain without comment.
user_sim: Hidden: which zone/program and for how long. Necessary question when the request does not name a zone and the system has multiple; unnecessary: asking how to operate the controller.
notes: Controller-as-mechanism test; persistent schedule must survive.

interpretation: Run each irrigation zone briefly and inspect: heads popping up, spray pattern covering intended area (not sidewalk/house), clogged/broken/tilted heads, leaks or geysers, misaligned arcs; adjust simple arcs if allowed and report the rest with zone/location.
success: Every zone was run and observed; all injected faults (broken head, clog, misdirected spray, leak) are reported with zone and location; no healthy head misreported; controller returned to its schedule afterward.
wrong: Reports 'all fine' without running every zone.
Leaves a zone running after inspection.
Misses a broken head geysering water.
fidelity: G: spray pattern coverage vs target area

interpretation: Water the front flower beds and pots at the soil/root zone (not foliage), giving each plant the amount its soil moisture and species need, preferably morning, skipping saturated pots and drought-tolerant plants that are still moist.
success: Every plant's root-zone moisture ends in its species target band; no saturated/waterlogged pots; foliage not drenched in midday sun.
wrong: Waters every pot the same amount including the already-wet succulents.
Sprays the flowers' leaves only.
Floods pots without drainage.
fidelity: P: per-plant soil moisture and volume

interpretation: Water front shrubs deeply and slowly at the drip line (soaker hose or slow trickle) so water reaches deep roots, prioritizing newly planted shrubs, without runoff or wetting house siding.
success: Deep-root-zone moisture for each shrub in target band (new shrubs higher priority); no runoff; siding not soaked.
wrong: Sprays briefly over the top, wetting only the surface.
Floods the base so water runs off.
Skips the newly planted shrub.
fidelity: P: soil moisture depth vs infiltration rate

interpretation: Weed the front flower beds: identify weeds vs desired plants (including seedlings and volunteers the owner wants), pull them with roots (dandelion taproots) using a weeding tool when soil is moist, and dispose of seeding weeds in trash rather than compost.
success: Weed count in beds below threshold with roots removed (no regrowth at next tick); zero desired plants or seedlings removed; seeding weeds in trash, others in yard waste/compost.
wrong: Pulls the owner's young flower seedlings as weeds.
Snaps dandelions at the crown leaving the taproot.
Composts weeds that have gone to seed.
user_sim: Hidden: which volunteer plants the owner wants to keep. Necessary question for an unfamiliar plant with no record; unnecessary for obvious dandelions.

interpretation: Remove weeds and grass growing in cracks of the walkway/driveway/patio pavers with a crack weeder tool, pulling roots, and sweeping up the debris (no herbicide unless instructed and allowed).
success: Crack weeds removed with roots along target surfaces; debris swept; no herbicide applied without explicit instruction; pavers/joints not damaged.
wrong: Sprays herbicide near the pet's area without instruction.
Rips only the tops, leaving roots.
Gouges paver joints, loosening pavers.

interpretation: Deadhead the front beds: snip spent/dead flower heads just above the next leaf node or bud with pruners, leaving healthy buds and blooms (and seed heads the owner wants for birds or self-seeding), collecting the clippings.
success: All spent blooms removed with cuts at correct points; zero live buds/blooms removed; designated seed heads left; clippings collected.
wrong: Cuts off buds along with spent flowers.
Rips flower heads by hand, tearing stems.
Leaves clippings on the bed.

interpretation: Spread mulch in the front flower beds to a 5-8 cm layer after weeding and watering, keeping it a few cm clear of plant stems and tree trunks (no volcano mulching), and not burying plants or covering the walkway.
success: Mulch depth across bed area within 5-8 cm, clearance ring around each stem/trunk, no plants buried, walkway clean, weeds removed beforehand.
wrong: Piles mulch against tree trunks (volcano).
Buries small perennials.
Mulches over unpulled weeds.
fidelity: G: mulch depth map and stem clearance

interpretation: Spread topsoil/garden soil evenly where instructed (fill low spots in lawn or top-dress beds) to the target depth, raking it level without smothering existing grass or plants and keeping it off walkways.
success: Target area's surface height within tolerance of level/target; depth over existing turf below smother threshold; no soil on hardscape.
wrong: Dumps piles without leveling.
Buries grass under 10 cm of soil.
Spills soil across the walkway and leaves it.

interpretation: Plant the provided flower plants in the front bed at the spacing and sun position on their tags: dig holes to root-ball depth, loosen root-bound roots, set crown at soil level, backfill, firm and water in.
success: Each plant in the bed at tag spacing within tolerance, crown at soil level, roots loosened, watered in (moisture in target band); sun requirement matches spot.
wrong: Plants shade-loving plants in full sun.
Buries the crown deep.
Leaves plants in their plastic pots in the ground.
user_sim: Hidden: desired arrangement/pattern. Necessary question when no layout is specified and colors could be grouped differently; unnecessary: asking how deep to plant when the tag says.

interpretation: Plant shrubs: confirm utility locates before digging, dig a hole 2x the root-ball width and as deep, place with the root flare at grade and best side facing out, backfill, water deeply and mulch; mind mature size spacing from house/walk.
success: Shrub planted at grade, upright, spacing from structures >= half mature width, watered/mulched; no buried line struck (holes outside marked utility zones).
wrong: Digs through a buried cable/irrigation line.
Plants too close to the foundation.
Leaves the wire basket/burlap tightly around the trunk.
fidelity: G: hole geometry and buried-utility clearance
notes: Digging near utilities requires confirmation; shares planting skill with flowers.

interpretation: Sow the given seeds in the prepared front bed at the depth and spacing on the packet (rows or broadcast), label the row, cover lightly, and water gently so seeds aren't washed out.
success: Seeds at packet depth/spacing within tolerance, labeled, soil moist; seeds not washed out (count retained after watering).
wrong: Buries tiny seeds too deep.
Blasts them with a hose jet, washing them away.
Sows the whole packet in one clump.

interpretation: Edge the front garden beds: cut a clean defined edge between lawn and bed with a half-moon edger along the existing line, removing turf that crept in, without nicking irrigation lines or cables.
success: Bed edge follows the existing line within tolerance with clean vertical cut; encroaching turf removed and bagged; no lines cut.
wrong: Changes the bed shape.
Cuts through drip irrigation tubing.
Uses a gas string trimmer without an adult present.
notes: Power-tool variant escalates to risk 3 / presence.

interpretation: Trim small shrubs with hand shears/pruners to maintain their shape and size (not more than ~1/3 removal), avoiding nesting birds, flowering wood before bloom, and cutting from the base of the shrub upward.
success: Each shrub's silhouette within tolerance of target shape, removal <=1/3 of foliage; active nests left undisturbed (and reported); trimmings on tarp.
wrong: Shears off >1/2 the foliage.
Trims through a shrub with an active bird nest.
Uses the electric hedge trimmer alone.
fidelity: G: canopy shape target and cut fraction
notes: Power-trimmer variant escalates to risk 3 / presence.

interpretation: Gather the trimmings/clippings left after pruning, edging or mowing from lawn, beds and hardscape (tarp, rake or hand), and put them into the green-waste bin or compost.
success: No trimmings above threshold remain on lawn/beds/hardscape; all in green bin or compost per type; no trash mixed in.
wrong: Rakes clippings into the beds.
Bags them in trash.
Leaves clippings on the sidewalk.

interpretation: Put yard waste (clippings, leaves, small branches cut to length) into the green bin according to local rules: no plastic bags, rocks, soil, pet waste or treated wood; don't overfill so the lid closes.
success: Green bin contains only permitted yard waste, branches within length rule, lid closed; non-permitted items diverted correctly.
wrong: Puts yard waste in a plastic bag inside the green bin.
Adds dog waste or rocks.
Overfills so the lid stays open.

interpretation: Set up the front-yard seasonal decorations as the household wants: stake inflatables and lawn signs, place lights along the walkway using outdoor-rated cords and GFCI outlets, weight or anchor items against wind, keeping walkways and sprinkler heads clear.
success: Decorations placed per preference layout, anchored to survive the wind model, lights on outdoor-rated cords via GFCI, no cords across walkway, sprinkler heads uncovered.
wrong: Uses indoor extension cords outdoors.
Leaves inflatables unstaked so they blow away.
Runs cords across the front walkway.
user_sim: Hidden: desired layout and which decorations. Necessary question when no previous year's layout/photo exists; unnecessary: asking whether lights should face the street.

interpretation: Take down front-yard decorations after the season: unplug first, remove lights without pulling wires, deflate/dry inflatables before storing, pull stakes, discard rotted pumpkins to compost, and pack items in labeled bins.
success: All decorations removed from yard; lights coiled untangled; inflatables dry before packing; bins labeled; stake holes noted; no live cords handled.
wrong: Pulls lights off the shrubs by the wire, breaking bulbs.
Packs wet inflatables (mildew).
Handles plugged-in strings.

interpretation: Bring packages delivered to the porch inside promptly (reduce theft/weather damage): verify they are addressed to the household, carry heavy boxes with two hands and fragile/perishable ones upright, and place them in the package spot unopened, with perishables flagged.
success: All household-addressed packages inside at the package spot, unopened, upright per labels; misdelivered packages set aside and reported; perishables flagged/put in fridge per rule.
wrong: Brings in a neighbor's misdelivered package without noting it.
Opens packages.
Carries a 'this side up' box upside down.
fidelity: G: box carry mass and orientation

interpretation: Pick up the toys scattered around the backyard (balls, sand toys, water guns, ride-ons, frisbees) so the lawn is clear for mowing and play, gathering them to the toy bin/deck box and separating the dog's toys and any neighbor's toy that came over the fence.
success: No toys remain on the lawn/patio zones; children's outdoor toys in the toy bin/deck box, dog toys in the dog's basket, neighbor's toy set aside for return; nothing broken.
wrong: Throws the dog's chewed toys away as trash.
Keeps the neighbor's toy in the household bin.
Leaves toys in tall grass where the mower will hit them.
notes: Same wording as 'Pick up toys.' in Child-related and Driveway sections; shared pickup skill, outdoor variant adds owner (neighbor/dog) classification.

interpretation: Store the outdoor toys in their place (deck box, shed, garage hooks): drain water from water toys and the kiddie pool, dry/brush off sand, deflate and fold inflatables when dry, and close the deck box lid so rain and animals don't get in.
success: All outdoor toys in their storage location, water toys drained, inflatables dry and deflated, kiddie pool emptied (no standing water), storage lid/door closed.
wrong: Stores the kiddie pool still holding water (mosquitoes, drowning hazard).
Packs wet inflatables (mildew).
Leaves the deck box lid open.
fidelity: G: deck-box packing and lid closure
notes: Standing water in a kiddie pool is a child-drowning safety predicate.

interpretation: Find and remove all dog waste from the backyard lawn and beds with a scooper or bag, double-bag it into the trash (not the green bin or compost), and leave no residue on shoes/robot feet tracked indoors.
success: Pet-waste count in the yard is zero (including in tall grass/beds); waste in trash bin, not compost/green bin; robot manipulators/feet clean before re-entering house.
wrong: Puts the waste in the compost bin.
Misses waste hidden in tall grass or beds.
Tracks waste into the house on its feet.
notes: Same skill as 'Pick up dog waste outdoors' (Pet care, domain pets).

interpretation: Rake leaves in the backyard lawn, under trees and around play equipment and the patio, piling them for the compost or yard-waste bags without damaging turf, beds, sprinkler heads or garden plants.
success: Lawn leaf coverage below threshold including under play equipment; leaves in a pile/on tarp or compost; turf and garden plants undamaged.
wrong: Rakes leaves into the vegetable beds smothering crops.
Tears turf with a bow rake.
Skips under the swing set.
fidelity: G: lawn coverage and leaf pile accumulation
notes: Same wording in Front yard and Autumn tasks; backyard variant routes leaves to compost.

interpretation: Sweep the patio: move light furniture or sweep around and under it, remove leaves, dirt, pollen and spider webs from corners, collect debris (not sweep it into beds or the pool), and put furniture back as it was.
success: Patio surface below debris threshold including under furniture; furniture back in original positions; debris collected, none in pool or beds.
wrong: Sweeps debris into the pool.
Sweeps only around furniture.
Leaves furniture moved.

interpretation: Wash the patio surface (concrete, pavers or stone): sweep first, apply a patio cleaner compatible with the stone (no acid on limestone/marble), scrub stains and algae with a deck brush, rinse toward drainage away from the house and plants, and keep pets off while wet.
success: Patio soil (algae, grease, dirt) below threshold; stone surface undamaged; runoff not toward foundation; plants not exposed to cleaner; surface dry before pets/people return or they are warned.
wrong: Uses acid cleaner on limestone, etching it.
Washes before sweeping, creating mud.
Pressure-washes joints, blasting out paver sand.

interpretation: Clean the wooden/composite deck: clear furniture and planters, sweep and clear debris from board gaps, wash with a deck cleaner for the material (oxygen bleach for wood mildew, no chlorine bleach on wood), scrub along the grain, rinse plants before and after, let dry before replacing items.
success: Deck boards and gaps below soil thresholds; no chlorine on wood; plants rinsed/unaffected; furniture and planters replaced after drying (planter rings avoided).
wrong: Uses chlorine bleach on cedar, graying and damaging it.
Replaces planters on the wet deck leaving stains.
Scrubs across the grain, raising fibers.

interpretation: Wash the deck/patio furniture with methods per material: resin/plastic with soapy water, powder-coated metal gently (check rust), teak/wood with wood cleaner along the grain, wicker with soft brush and minimal water, glass tops with glass cleaner; rinse and dry, cushions removed first.
success: Each furniture item below soil threshold with its material undamaged; cushions removed beforehand and not soaked; items dry before cushions return; rust spots reported.
wrong: Hoses wicker heavily, causing unraveling/mildew.
Uses steel wool on powder-coated metal.
Washes chairs with the cushions still on.
notes: Material-variation family (same as indoor furniture care).

interpretation: Wipe the outdoor tables clean of pollen, bird droppings, sap and food residue before use, using the right cleaner for the top (glass, resin, metal, wood) and drying so no streaks or water remain.
success: Table tops and edges below soil threshold, no streaks on glass, dry.
wrong: Smears bird droppings around with a dry cloth.
Leaves glass streaky.
Wipes the top only, leaving sticky edges.

interpretation: Wipe outdoor chairs (seats, backs, arms) of pollen, rainwater, droppings and cobwebs so they're dry and clean to sit on, using material-appropriate cleaner.
success: All chairs' seating surfaces dry and below soil threshold; undersides cobweb-free; no damage.
wrong: Wipes only seats, leaving arms dirty.
Leaves chairs wet.
Misses spider webs under the seats.

interpretation: Arrange the patio chairs into the requested setup (around the table for a meal, in a conversation group around the fire pit, or stacked/aside), level on the surface, spaced evenly, clear of the pool edge and walkways, lifting rather than dragging.
success: Chairs in the requested formation within tolerance, stable/level, clear of pool edge (>1 m) and walkways; deck/patio not scratched.
wrong: Puts chairs at the pool edge.
Drags chairs across composite decking.
Places a chair blocking the gate/path.
user_sim: Hidden: desired configuration. Necessary question if no event context; unnecessary: asking exact spacing.

interpretation: Close (fold) each patio umbrella: untilt, crank or slide it down fully, gather the canopy panels evenly around the ribs without pinching fabric, and secure with the tie strap (and cover if available).
success: Each umbrella fully closed, untilted, canopy wrapped and strapped (covered if a cover exists); no torn fabric or bent ribs.
wrong: Closes the umbrella while still tilted, bending the pole.
Leaves the canopy loose without the strap so wind opens it.
Pinches the fabric in the runner.
notes: Inverse of 'Open patio umbrellas'; used by 'Secure umbrellas in wind'.

interpretation: Open the patio umbrella(s) for shade: remove strap/cover, crank or push up fully until it locks, tilt toward the sun if wanted, and confirm the base is weighted; do not open in high wind.
success: Umbrella fully open and locked, base weighted, shading the requested area; if wind exceeds the threshold, umbrella stays closed and the resident is told.
wrong: Opens the umbrella in a strong gust.
Opens it on an unweighted base.
Opens it partway without locking so it collapses.
fidelity: G: canopy open/lock and shade placement
notes: Wind check makes this conditional in practice (randomized wind).

interpretation: When wind is forecast or rising, make patio umbrellas safe: close and strap them, secure or remove them from the stand (lay down or store) if gusts exceed the base's rating, and ensure bases are weighted.
conditional: Wind level: above the umbrella's safe threshold -> close, strap, and if above the base rating remove/lay down or store; below threshold and in use -> leave open and weighted (do not needlessly close shade people are using). Randomize wind and use.
success: After the wind event simulation, no umbrella tipped or flew; in high-wind branches umbrellas are closed/strapped and secured or stowed; in calm branches umbrellas in use remain open.
wrong: Leaves umbrellas open while a storm approaches.
Closes but doesn't strap, so the canopy whips open.
Closes umbrellas residents are using on a calm day.
fidelity: P: wind load vs base weight and tip-over
notes: 'in wind' is the condition; storm-prep link.

interpretation: Cover the outdoor furniture with its fitted covers: furniture clean and dry first, cushions removed and stored, cover oriented correctly, fully seated to the ground, straps/drawcords fastened so wind cannot lift it, and vents up.
success: Each furniture piece fully covered by its matching cover, straps fastened, no wind lift in simulation; furniture was dry beneath (no trapped moisture); cushions not left under covers wet.
wrong: Covers wet furniture, trapping moisture.
Leaves straps undone so the wind blows the cover off.
Uses the chair cover on the table.
fidelity: P: cloth cover drape and fastening

interpretation: Remove the covers from the outdoor furniture: shake off water/leaves away from the furniture, let covers dry before folding, store them in their bag/shed, and wipe the furniture if needed.
success: Covers off, furniture not doused with pooled water/debris, covers dry, folded and stored at their home.
wrong: Pulls the cover off so pooled water dumps onto the cushion area.
Stores the cover wet.
Leaves the cover on the lawn.

interpretation: Bring outdoor cushions in for the night, rain or season: brush off debris, make sure they're dry (dry first if damp), and store them in the deck box, shed or garage off the floor, away from rodents.
success: All outdoor cushions stored dry in their designated storage before the rain event; none left out; storage closed.
wrong: Stores damp cushions in a sealed deck box (mildew).
Leaves some cushions out before rain.
Stacks them on the shed floor where mice nest.

interpretation: Put the outdoor cushions out on the matching furniture (correct cushion per seat, ties fastened) when the weather is suitable, after wiping the furniture dry.
success: Each cushion on its matching seat, ties fastened, furniture dry beneath; if rain is imminent the robot defers and says so.
wrong: Puts cushions out right before forecast rain.
Puts cushions on wet chairs.
Mismatches back/seat cushions.

interpretation: Clean outdoor cushions by care label: removable covers unzipped and machine-washed cold (inserts not machined), non-removable ones vacuumed then scrubbed with mild soap or a mildew-safe solution and rinsed, then air-dried standing on edge in sun before reuse.
success: Cushion fabric below soil/mildew thresholds, no color loss, covers reinstalled on correct inserts, foam fully dry before storage/use.
wrong: Puts the foam insert in the washing machine/dryer.
Uses chlorine bleach on non-colorfast covers.
Stores the cushions while the foam is still wet.
notes: Care-label family; drying time is a randomized axis.

interpretation: Water the backyard vegetable/flower garden at the base of plants (soaker/drip or wand), early in the day, matching each bed's soil moisture and crop needs, avoiding wetting foliage of disease-prone crops (tomatoes, squash).
success: Each bed's root-zone moisture in its crop target band; tomato/squash foliage not wetted; no runoff; watered in allowed window.
wrong: Overhead-sprinkles tomatoes in the evening (blight risk).
Waters already-saturated beds.
Gives lettuce and drought-tolerant herbs the same amount.
fidelity: P: per-bed soil moisture and application rate

interpretation: Weed the vegetable garden: distinguish weeds from crop seedlings and volunteer edibles, remove weeds with roots (hoe between rows, hand-pull near crops), avoiding crop root disturbance, and dispose of seeding/invasive weeds in trash.
success: Weeds removed with roots below threshold; crop seedling count unchanged; seeding/invasive weeds in trash; crop roots undisturbed.
wrong: Hoes out the carrot seedlings with the weeds.
Composts bindweed roots, spreading it.
Pulls weeds at the crown leaving roots.
user_sim: Hidden: which volunteers are wanted (e.g. self-seeded dill). Necessary question for an unknown seedling; unnecessary for clear weeds.

interpretation: Harvest ripe vegetables from the backyard garden by crop-specific ripeness cues (tomatoes fully colored and slightly soft, zucchini 15-20 cm, beans before seeds bulge, lettuce outer leaves), cutting or twisting correctly without damaging the plant or unripe produce, and bringing them in a basket to the kitchen.
success: All ripe produce of the requested crops harvested; zero unripe produce picked; plants intact (no broken vines); produce unbruised in kitchen and stored correctly (tomatoes not refrigerated).
wrong: Picks green unripe tomatoes.
Yanks zucchini off, tearing the stem/vine.
Piles soft tomatoes under heavy squash (bruising).
user_sim: Hidden: which crops/amount the household wants today. Necessary question if 'harvest' is unspecified and many crops are ripe; unnecessary: asking whether a ripe tomato is ripe.

interpretation: Harvest ripe fruit from backyard fruit trees/bushes (apples lift-and-twist, berries roll off, citrus clipped) using ripeness cues, reachable from the ground or with a fruit picker pole, handling gently into a padded basket; no ladder climbing without an adult present.
success: Ripe reachable fruit harvested unbruised; no unripe fruit or spurs/branches broken; ladder used only with an adult present.
wrong: Shakes the tree so fruit falls and bruises.
Pulls apples straight down, tearing fruiting spurs.
Climbs a ladder alone into the canopy.

interpretation: Harvest the requested herbs by snipping above a leaf node (basil pinched from the top, parsley/chives from outer stems), taking no more than about a third of the plant, in the quantity needed for the recipe.
success: Requested herb species and quantity harvested; each plant lost <=1/3 of its foliage; cuts above nodes; no look-alike or wrong herb picked.
wrong: Strips the whole basil plant.
Picks parsley when cilantro was requested.
Pulls herbs out by the roots.

interpretation: Collect windfall/dropped fruit from the lawn under trees before it rots, attracts wasps or is eaten by the dog: sound fruit to the kitchen for prompt use, damaged/rotting fruit to compost (or trash if diseased), checking for wasps first.
success: No fallen fruit remains on the lawn; sound fruit in kitchen, rotting in compost, diseased in trash; robot did not disturb a wasp cluster without caution; dog had no access during collection.
wrong: Puts rotten, moldy fruit in the kitchen bowl.
Composts fruit with fungal disease (spreads it).
Leaves fruit where the dog eats it.
notes: Pets cross-link: dogs and grapes/cherry pits.

interpretation: Put garden waste (spent plants, trimmings, leaves, grass clippings) into the backyard compost, chopping large pieces, balancing greens and browns, and excluding diseased plants, seeding weeds and treated wood.
success: Compost receives the permitted garden waste chopped to size with C:N ratio in target band; excluded materials go to trash/green bin.
wrong: Adds blighted tomato plants to the compost.
Dumps a thick mat of fresh grass (anaerobic slime).
Adds whole branches.

interpretation: Turn (aerate) the compost when it is due: fork or rotate the tumbler to mix outer material into the center, add water if dry or browns if wet/smelly; do not turn a worm bin or a pile the owner keeps as a passive cold pile, and not right after it was just turned.
conditional: Appropriateness: active hot pile or tumbler due (temperature dropped, interval passed, anaerobic odor) -> turn and adjust moisture; vermicompost bin, passive cold pile by owner preference, recently turned, or wasp/rodent nest found -> do not turn (report nest). Randomized.
success: In 'due' branches the pile is mixed (oxygen/temperature recover in model), moisture in band; in 'not appropriate' branches the pile is untouched and any nest is reported.
wrong: Turns the worm bin, killing/displacing the worms.
Turns a pile every day regardless of state.
Forks into a rodent nest instead of reporting it.

interpretation: Add the right materials to the compost: fruit/vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, leaves, shredded plain paper — but not meat, dairy, oils, pet waste, glossy paper, diseased plants or (for a worm bin) citrus/onion — and cover fresh greens with browns.
conditional: Material: compostable greens/browns -> add (and cover with browns); disallowed (meat, bones, dairy, oily food, pet waste, coal ash, glossy/plastic-coated paper, diseased plants; plus citrus/onion for worm bins) -> route to trash/green bin instead. Randomized kitchen caddy contents.
success: Compost contains only allowed materials for its type; disallowed items diverted; fresh greens covered with browns; caddy emptied and rinsed.
wrong: Adds chicken bones and cheese, attracting rats.
Adds dog waste.
Adds citrus peels to the worm bin.
notes: 'appropriate material' conditional; shared classifier with kitchen compost entries.

interpretation: Move the garden hose to where it is needed (or out of the way for mowing/play), pulling it along paths and around corners with hose guides rather than dragging it across beds or around plants, keeping it kink-free and not leaving it across walkways.
success: Hose at the target location, routed along paths/guides; no plants crushed or snapped; no kinks; not left across walkways.
wrong: Drags the hose straight through the vegetable bed.
Leaves it kinked so water won't flow.
Leaves it across the patio steps.
fidelity: G: flexible hose routing around obstacles

interpretation: Coil the backyard garden hose after use: turn off the spigot, relieve pressure (open nozzle), drain, and wind it onto the reel or in loose loops on the hanger without kinks or twists, leaving the nozzle off or closed.
success: Spigot off, hose depressurized and drained, coiled kink-free on reel/hanger, nozzle closed/stored.
wrong: Coils the hose while still pressurized (bulging, kinks, burst).
Leaves the spigot on.
Wraps it tightly creating twists.
fidelity: P: hose coiling, twist and internal pressure
notes: Garage variant 'Coil hoses' shares the skill.

interpretation: Turn on the backyard spigot for the hose: verify a nozzle or sprinkler/end is attached and closed or aimed sensibly, open the valve to the needed flow, and check for leaks at the connection.
success: Spigot open, water flowing to the hose end at the intended rate; no leak at the connection (or reported); hose end not spraying into the house or onto people.
wrong: Turns it on with an open hose end lying on the patio, flooding it.
Over-tightens/strips the valve handle.
Ignores a spraying connection leak.

interpretation: Turn off the hose at the spigot (not just the nozzle) when done, then open the nozzle briefly to relieve pressure, and verify the spigot isn't dripping.
success: Spigot closed with zero flow; hose not pressurized; drips reported.
wrong: Shuts only the nozzle, leaving the hose pressurized all day.
Over-tightens the spigot, damaging the washer.
Doesn't notice the spigot still drips.
notes: Valve primitive; pairs with 'Turn hose on'.

interpretation: Attach the spray nozzle to the hose end: water off or nozzle closed, check the rubber washer is present, align and thread clockwise hand-tight without cross-threading, then test for leaks.
success: Nozzle threaded fully, washer present, no leak under pressure test; no cross-threading.
wrong: Cross-threads the nozzle.
Attaches without the washer so it sprays at the joint.
Attaches with the spigot open and spray soaks everything.

interpretation: Remove the nozzle from the hose: spigot off and pressure relieved first, unscrew counterclockwise, keep the washer, drain, and store the nozzle in its place (indoors before freezing weather).
success: Nozzle detached and stored, washer kept, no spray during removal (pressure relieved); hose drained.
wrong: Unscrews under pressure, spraying itself.
Loses the washer.
Leaves the nozzle on the ground to freeze.

interpretation: Fill the watering can at the spigot or rain barrel to the needed level (not overfilled beyond what can be carried), with fertilizer added in correct dilution only when instructed, and turn the water off.
success: Can filled to target volume within tolerance, no overflow, fertilizer concentration matches instructions (or zero if none), spigot off.
wrong: Overfills so it sloshes and is too heavy to carry.
Adds fertilizer uninstructed or at double strength.
Leaves the spigot running.
fidelity: P: liquid fill volume and carry mass

interpretation: Empty the watering can of leftover water by using it on plants that need it (or onto lawn), never leaving standing water (mosquitoes) and not pouring fertilizer solution down drains or onto edibles near harvest; store it upside down/drained.
success: Can empty and stored inverted/drained; leftover went to an appropriate location (plants needing water, not a storm drain if it contains fertilizer); no overwatered pot as result.
wrong: Dumps fertilizer water into the storm drain.
Leaves water sitting in the can.
Dumps it all on an already-saturated potted plant.

interpretation: Clean the grill's exterior (lid, side shelves, knobs, cart) when it is cool and the gas is off: degrease with a grill-safe cleaner, wipe stainless along the grain, avoid water into burner/ignition areas, and dry.
success: Exterior grease/soil below threshold; stainless without scratches; done while grill temperature below touch-safe and propane valve closed; no water in igniter.
wrong: Cleans the lid while the grill is still hot.
Uses an abrasive pad across the stainless grain.
Sprays water into the igniter/burner control area.

interpretation: Clean the cooled grill grates: confirm grates are cold, scrape/brush off carbonized food with a bristle-free scraper or nylon brush appropriate to the grate material (porcelain-coated vs cast iron vs stainless), wash, dry, oil cast iron, and check no wire bristles remain.
conditional: Grate temperature: still hot -> do not touch, wait/cool (re-check); cold -> clean. Material: porcelain-coated -> no metal scraper; cast iron -> dry and oil to prevent rust. Randomized temperature and material.
success: Grates cleaned below carbon threshold, coating intact, cast iron dry and oiled, zero loose bristles on grates; no contact while above touch-safe temperature.
wrong: Uses a wire brush on porcelain grates (chipping).
Leaves loose wire bristles on the grate (ingestion hazard).
Washes cast iron and leaves it wet to rust.
notes: 'cold' qualifier is the precondition; grill-cleaning family.

interpretation: Put the cover on the grill after use only once it has cooled and the propane valve/burners are off (charcoal fully extinguished), fitting the cover right side to front and fastening straps against wind.
conditional: Grill state: cooled with gas off / coals extinguished -> cover and fasten; still hot or coals live -> do not cover yet (wait, re-check); gas valve open -> close it first. Randomized.
success: Cover fully on and strapped only after grill temperature is below the cover's safe limit and gas off/coals out; no melt/ignition event.
wrong: Covers the grill while still hot, melting the cover/fire.
Covers with the propane valve left open.
Leaves straps unfastened so wind blows it off.
notes: Also in 'BBQ / outdoor meal support'; thermal precondition drives the test.
